title: Assignee silently cleared when status advances past `assigned` — `body.assignee` excluded from save payload for all other statuses
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-22 and conclusively resolved (previously cannot_verify across two runs). The old architecture that could have exhibited this bug no longer exists: status changes and assignee changes are now fully separate code paths. `audit-assurance.controller.js`'s `updateScopeItem` (the plain PUT endpoint) explicitly REJECTS any `assessmentStatus` in its body (lines 1071-1076) and only ever touches `assignee` when the key is present, independent of status (lines 1094-1102: `if (assignee !== undefined) { item.assignee = assignee || null; ... }`). Status changes instead go through `POST /api/workflows/audit_scope_item/:id/transition`, whose `WorkflowTransitionService.transition()` only touches `assignee` when the target state is `assigned`/`re-assign` AND an `assignedTo` is explicitly supplied (workflow/workflowTransition.service.js lines 179-204) — for every other target status it never reads or writes the assignee field. Frontend `ScopeItemDetailDrawer.jsx`'s `handleSave` (lines 911-916) also unconditionally includes `assignee: assignee || null` in every PUT payload. No code path can silently clear or omit assignee based on the target status.

```

title: N+1 query in `listScopeItems` — Mongoose `.populate()` issues one user query per scope item; 100-item page = 100 queries
fixEvidence: Re-verified 2026-08-22 — claim not reproducible against current code. `audit-assurance.controller.js`'s `listScopeItems()` (lines 844-892) uses Mongoose's standard batched `.populate([...])` (lines 871-875 for assignee/assignedBy/frameworkId), which issues a single `$in` query per populated path across the whole result set, not one query per document — this is not an N+1 pattern by construction. The polymorphic `requirementId` population (lines 883-892) is likewise batched via two `$in` queries (legacy vs FrameworkRequirement items), and linked-resource counts are resolved via `requirement-resource-resolver.service.js`'s batched helpers. A 100-item page produces roughly 6-7 total queries, not 100. Either this was fixed in an earlier, undocumented change, or the original defect mischaracterized Mongoose's populate() behaviour.

title: No role-specific permissions (`audit.approve`, `audit.lead_auditor`) — no enforced separation of auditor vs. approver vs. manager
description:
Files: All `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/audit-assurance/routes/` files

Re-verified 2026-08-22 — claim is partially outdated but the underlying concern still holds. `audit.approve` DOES now exist and is enforced (`routes/governance.routes.js:45-48` gates report approve/reject/publish/archive with it) — the literal "no audit.approve" claim is false. `audit.lead_auditor` was never a realistic permission shape in this system (permissions are strictly `module.action` from a fixed 6-action list: read/create/update/delete/approve/admin — there's no custom per-role permission mechanism), so that half reflects a misunderstanding of the permission model rather than a gap. That said, the structural concern remains: across the module roughly 116 route bindings use the single broad `audit.update` and only 4 use `audit.approve` (all in governance reports) — CAR verification, closure approve/reject (see H-004), findings CRUD, etc. are all still gated by the same flat `audit.update`, so there is no permission-level separation of auditor/approver/manager for those flows (only ad-hoc in-code segregation-of-duty checks like requestor≠approver in audit-closure.service.js and assignee≠verifier in corrective-action.service.js).

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix M-010: extend the existing audit.approve permission (already used by governance.routes.js) to also gate audit-closure.routes.js's approve/reject/request-approval (see H-004) and corrective-action.routes.js's verify endpoint, instead of introducing a new non-standard audit.lead_auditor permission.
```

```

title: Evidence attachment stores `evidenceId` reference only — vault document modifiable post-approval; approved evidence and referenced document can diverge
description:
Files: `audit-scope-item.model.js`'s `evidenceAttachmentSchema` (lines 210-223), `corrective-action.service.js`'s `uploadEvidenceFile()` (lines 554-665)

Re-verified 2026-08-22 and confirmed still open, worse than originally described for the CAR path specifically. `evidenceAttachmentSchema` stores `evidenceId` (ref), `verdict`, `reviewedBy/At` — no content hash/version pin captured at approval time. `corrective-action.service.js`'s `uploadEvidenceFile()` uploads to S3 and creates an `Evidence` doc directly, bypassing the standard evidence-upload worker, with NO checksum computed at all — confirmed by contrast with `evidence/evidence-upload.worker.js` (lines 114-115, 193-199), which does compute a real SHA-256 (`S3.computeChecksum(buffer)`) for evidence uploaded through the normal Evidence Repository flow. `evidence.model.js` already has a `checksum {algorithm, value}` schema field, proving the platform has the capability — it's just not wired into the CAR evidence path, and even where a checksum exists elsewhere, nothing re-validates it before/at approval or prevents silent replacement of the underlying S3 object post-approval (the S3 key is a stable pointer to a mutable object; no versionId pinning or object-lock is enforced anywhere in this module).

Claude Fix Prompt:
```
Fix M-012 in corrective-action.service.js's uploadEvidenceFile() and the scope item/CAR evidence schemas.

1. Compute a SHA-256 checksum of the uploaded buffer at upload time (reuse S3.computeChecksum from evidence-upload.worker.js) and store it on both the CAR's embedded evidence subdocument and the linked Evidence document.
2. On approval/verification, re-fetch and re-hash the S3 object; if it doesn't match the stored checksum, block the action and surface a "document changed since attachment" warning.
3. For audit closure evidence specifically, make the checksum mandatory.
```

title: Coverage/gap data is a frozen creation-time snapshot from the same UCL source as /grc-framework, with no ongoing reconciliation mechanism
description:
AuditScopeItem.pclContext is populated at audit-creation time by requirement-resource-resolver.service.js, the same compliance-frameworks module that backs /grc-framework's live coverage view - so the two views are not calculating from divergent data sources at the moment of audit creation. However, audit-scope-item.model.js:15-30 documents that the snapshot is then frozen (lock.isLocked=true, lockedBy:'creation_snapshot') and explicitly described as what the audit shows going forward, even if the underlying resource's status later changes. The automated drift-detection service that used to flag such changes (pclSyncService) has been deleted, so new pcl_change locks are no longer created - the model's own comment calls the replacement 'dormant' and real drift-management 'future work'.

Auditor-facing breakage: for the life of any audit (often weeks to months), the coverage badges shown inside audit-assurance can silently diverge from the same control's live coverage in /grc-framework, and the platform has no running mechanism to detect or surface that divergence to the auditor.

title: Audit-assurance's scope-item/evidence/policy/vendor-review workflow transitions share the same unguarded `WorkflowTransitionService._updateEntityStatus` — third confirmed instance of the same platform-wide race condition
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 8.1 operational planning and control
description:
**Checklist row:** §6.4 — Race conditions on concurrent transitions handled: two actors transitioning the same record concurrently don't produce a corrupted or double-applied state.
**Files:** `audit-assurance.controller.js` calls the shared `WorkflowTransitionService` for scope-item resource-workflow, evidence-review, and policy/vendor-review transitions — the same service already found (this run and in prior runs) to build its final write via `_updateEntityStatus()` (`workflowTransition.service.js:418-463`), an unconditional `Model.updateOne({ _id }, { $set: { status } })` with no precondition on the `currentState` read earlier in `transition()` (lines 50-86). This is the third module-level confirmation of the exact same shared-service gap already logged as `PM-CHK-003` (policy-management) and `EM-CHK-002` (evidence-management) — filed separately here because it's this module's own concurrent-reviewer surface (e.g. two auditors independently transitioning the same `audit_evidence_review`/`audit_policy_review` entry) that is exposed to it, not a duplicate of either prior finding.
**Root Cause:** Same as `PM-CHK-003`/`EM-CHK-002` — no optimistic-concurrency mechanism exists anywhere in `WorkflowTransitionService`'s shared read-check-write sequence, for any `entityType` it drives.
**Impact:** Two auditors (or an auditor and an admin override) concurrently transitioning the same scope-item's evidence/policy/vendor review can both pass the allowed-transition check against the same stale state and both write — the later call silently wins with no conflict signal, leaving a `WorkflowEntry` audit-trail entry that doesn't match the record's real final status.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Same fix as `PM-CHK-003`/`EM-CHK-002` — this is one shared-service bug with three confirmed call sites, not three separate bugs. Fix once in `WorkflowTransitionService._updateEntityStatus` (`workflowTransition.service.js:418-463`): add the `currentState` precondition to the `updateOne` filter and reject with a 409 on a matched-count of zero (see the other two records' fix prompts for the exact patch) — this closes the gap for `policy`, `evidence`, `audit_scope_item`, `audit_evidence_review`, `audit_policy_review`, `audit_vendor_review`, and every other `entityType` this service drives, in one place.

title: Five audit-assurance pages have zero permission gating of any kind — no page-level `PermissionGate`, no component-level `usePermission` check — relying entirely on the backend to fail closed
description:
**Checklist row:** §1.2 — RBAC permission gates on every UI action: every create/update/delete/approve button — and per this checklist's broader intent, every page a permission model exists for — is wrapped in `PermissionGate`/`usePermission`, not left to the backend alone.
**Files:** Unlike the module's other 4 pages (`page.jsx`, `new-template/page.jsx`, `programme/page.jsx`, `templates/[templateId]/page.jsx`, each wrapped in a `<PermissionGate>`), these five render their content components directly with no `PermissionGate`, no `usePermission` hook, and no `layout.jsx` anywhere in `(private)/audit-assurance/` or `(detail)/audit-assurance/` providing a blanket gate — confirmed by grep for `PermissionGate`/`usePermission` returning zero matches in all five files and in `ConfiguredRequirementsContent.jsx` itself (the component `[id]/configured/page.jsx` renders).
**Root Cause:** These five routes were added without carrying over the `PermissionGate` wrapper pattern used consistently on the module's other pages — likely because each is reached via an in-app link/button already itself permission-gated elsewhere, so the gap was never hit through the normal navigation flow.
**Impact:** Not a data exposure — the underlying API calls (`auditAssuranceService.getScopeItem`, the reports/configure endpoints) still require `audit.read`/`audit.update` server-side, confirmed in this module's route file. But any authenticated user who navigates to one of these URLs directly (a guessable/bookmarked/shared link) with no `audit.*` permission at all sees a real page shell attempt to load before failing on the API call, instead of the immediate, clear 'you don't have access to this' the rest of the module gives — an inconsistent, confusing UX distinct from an authorization bypass.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Wrap each of the four `(private)/audit-assurance/...` pages in `<PermissionGate permission="audit.read" allowProjectGrant>...</PermissionGate>` (matching `templates/[templateId]/page.jsx`'s pattern, since these are audit-record pages, not compliance-catalog pages). For the `(detail)` route's client-side `ScopeItemDetailPage`, add a `usePermission('audit.read', { allowProjectGrant: true })` check and render the existing error `Center` state (already present in the component) when it fails, before calling `auditAssuranceService.getScopeItem`.

title: Page-level permission gates are inconsistent across sibling audit-assurance pages — the main list and Programme pages gate on `compliance.read`, while Templates gates on `audit.read`, though the backend for all of them actually requires `audit.*`
description:
**Checklist row:** §1.2 — RBAC permission gates on every UI action, consistent with what the backend actually enforces (this checklist item's underlying intent — a gate that doesn't match reality is as broken as no gate).
**Files:** `page.jsx:8`, `new-template/page.jsx:8`, and `programme/page.jsx:10` all gate on `<PermissionGate permission="compliance.read" allowProjectGrant>`. `templates/[templateId]/page.jsx:10` instead gates on `<PermissionGate permission="audit.read" allowProjectGrant>`. But `audit-assurance.routes.js` — confirmed exhaustively in this module's prior checklist run — gates essentially every read endpoint in this module (scope items, findings, evidence, reports, the audit itself) on `requirePermission('audit.read')`, not `compliance.read`; `compliance.read` is the permission string owned by the separate `/grc-framework` / `client-compliance` module.
**Root Cause:** The main list, new-template, and Programme pages were gated with the wrong module's permission string at some point (`compliance.read` instead of `audit.read`) — plausibly copy-pasted from a `/grc-framework` page — while `templates/[templateId]/page.jsx` was built correctly.
**Impact:** Two failure directions: (1) a user who holds `audit.read` (the permission this module's own backend actually checks, and the one a Custom Project Role would realistically be given for audit access) but not `compliance.read` is blocked at the page gate from ever seeing `/audit-assurance`, `/audit-assurance/new-template`, or `/audit-assurance/programme` at all, despite being fully authorized against the real backend; (2) a user who holds `compliance.read` but not `audit.read` sees these three pages render past the gate, only to have every data call inside them fail — the opposite inconsistency from `AA-CHK-003`, but the same root problem: the frontend gate doesn't reflect the backend's real permission model.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Change `permission="compliance.read"` to `permission="audit.read"` in `page.jsx:8`, `new-template/page.jsx:8`, and `programme/page.jsx:10`, matching `templates/[templateId]/page.jsx`'s already-correct gate and the backend's actual `requirePermission('audit.read')` checks in `audit-assurance.routes.js`.
